notes: Documents: CTE guidelines, Office of Student Conduct and Academic Integrity AI page, Graduate School GenAI principles; both coders agreed all three delegate. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance, mostly A encourage/permit vs B neutral on 'encouraged/should' advice to instructors and programs; resolved to neutral when the passage takes no position on AI use, restrict where AI is allowed only on conditions. (2) policy_type on neighbouring readings of one sentence (P31 vs P48 vs P120 for verify/review/plagiarism items; P24 vs P27 for marking AI text; P107 vs P10 for ask-first; P56/P70/P66 for the office mission; P57 vs P40 for the interview; P34 vs P35 for an example assignment); resolved by re-reading the sentence and choosing the type whose definition matches the duty stated. (3) phase and actor for statements about process or sanctions (general vs over-time, student vs admin), resolved by who the sentence addresses. (4) modality: 'should never' coded must-not by A, should-not by B (should-not); 'are encouraged' resolved to should. Unit granularity: A coded many more sample syllabus statements and example assignments on the integrity page (34 only-A units, 33 kept, one question heading dropped); B coded 12 only-B units (11 kept, one repeat dropped). Sample statements and example assignments are kept but flagged as sample in their why, since they are not USC rules. One matched pair (a sentence with a permission and a limit) was split into two final units, and one CTE sentence with two duties was split into two units, so the final file has 147 units. Changed anchors only where a coder's anchor was too short to stand alone.
